questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the common idiom: 'Under the weather'?

options.option_text: Standing outside during a heavy thunderstorm.
Feeling slightly ill or physically unwell.
Having a very bad mood due to the rain.
Wearing warm clothes for a cold winter day.

questions.explanation: If someone is 'under the weather', it means they are feeling sick or not completely healthy.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the idiom: 'Hit the nail on the head'?

options.option_text: To forcefully strike a person on their head. (alternative interpretation)
To successfully build a wooden house. (alternative interpretation)
To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.
To suddenly remember an important thought. (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' means to be exactly right about something or to state the exact truth of a situation.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the idiom: 'Burn the midnight oil'?

options.option_text: To accidentally cause a large fire at home.
To waste expensive fuel resources carelessly.
To sleep very deeply and peacefully.
To read or work late into the night.

questions.explanation: Before electric lighting, people used oil lamps. To 'burn the midnight oil' means to work or study late into the night.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the idiom: 'Barking up the wrong tree'?

options.option_text: To make a mistake in one's line of thought or to pursue a false lead.
To successfully hunt a wild animal in the forest. (alternative interpretation)
To angrily shout at an innocent person. (alternative interpretation)
To plant a seed in the wrong type of soil. (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: This idiom comes from hunting dogs that stand barking at the bottom of a tree where they think prey is hiding, but it has escaped. It means pursuing a false lead or looking in the wrong place.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the phrase: 'Let the cat out of the bag'?

options.option_text: To actively rescue a trapped animal.
To finally allow someone to have their freedom.
To reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake.
To physically open a heavy sealed container.

questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' means to disclose a secret that was supposed to be kept hidden.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the idiom: 'A damp squib'?

options.option_text: A very wet and completely miserable rainy day. (alternative interpretation)
A situation or event which is much less impressive than expected.
An explosive device that goes off dangerously early.
A person who constantly complains about everything.

questions.explanation: A 'squib' is a small firework. If it is damp, it won't explode properly. Thus, a 'damp squib' is something that fails completely to meet expectations.

questions.stem: What is the exact correct meaning of the phrase: 'To read between the lines'?

options.option_text: To read a document very quickly by skipping entire sentences. (alternative interpretation)
To physically highlight the blank spaces on a printed paper. (alternative interpretation)
To completely misunderstand the obvious main plot of a novel. (alternative interpretation)
To look for or discover a meaning that is hidden or implied rather than explicitly stated.

questions.explanation: To 'read between the lines' means to infer a meaning that is not explicitly stated in a text or situation, understanding the hidden intent or emotion.
